title: Polarized vs. Threshold Training Intensity Distribution on Endurance Sport Performance: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: Rosenblat MA, Perrotta AS, Vicenzino B
journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
population: Endurance-trained athletes (>2 years training, VO2max/peak >50 mL/kg/min); RCTs comparing polarized with threshold TID
findings: Search to 6 November 2016 gave 329 results; 4 RCTs met inclusion (3 pooled); PEDro scores 4/10 (two studies) and 5/10 (two studies).
Pooled time-trial effect favoured polarized over threshold: ES = -0.66 (95% CI -1.17 to -0.15).
Authors conclude polarized may lead to greater improvement than threshold.
limitations: Three pooled studies of low PEDro quality, mixed sports; compares polarized with threshold only (not pyramidal); search ended 2016 and later syntheses supersede it. Evidence level lowered from A to B because the underlying trials are few and low quality.
implications: Supports not making a threshold-dominant (zone 2 > zone 1) distribution the default; this is the most consistent finding in the literature.
Do not cite it as evidence that polarized beats pyramidal.

verification.notes: Crossref matches JSCR Dec 2019. Total n not stated in abstract, left null. Level downgraded A to B.
